# video-gen

Imported as `@elffuss/ai/video-gen`, `@elffuss/ai/video-gen/sizes`.

## `sdk/video-gen/estimate.js`

Whether this device can make a video, before anything is downloaded: the WebGPU adapter (a real one, with shader-f16, and buffers as large as the largest tensor of the run), the memory the run needs at its peak, and the download (all of it, and what the model store does not have yet). The memory figures come from measured runs of the graphs (see the numbers below); a device that does not say how much memory it has is probed by asking WebGPU for buffers of that size and giving them back at once, never assumed.

### `peakBytes({ tokens, width, height }, { ditBytes, encoderShardBytes, embedBytes, decoderBytes })`

Bytes the run holds at its peak, by phase, for a number of tokens. The
transformer phase holds its weights (`ditBytes`), the prompt's keys and
values, and per token the residual stream, the attention's copies of keys and
values and the feed-forward's widest tensor.

### `largestBuffer({ tokens, width, height })`

The largest single buffer of a run: the feed-forward's hidden tensor, or the decoder's widest.

### `estimate(opts = {}, env = {})`

Can this device make the video `opts` asks for, and what would it download?
Downloads nothing. Without a store, `missingBytes` is the whole download.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `[opts]` | `{ seconds?: number, size?: string, steps?: number }` |  |
| `[env]` | `{ registry?: object, registryUrl?: string, model?: string, store?: { has(url: string, bytes: number): Promise<boolean> }, gpu?: any, probeMemory?: boolean }` |  |

Returns `Promise<{ fits: boolean, reason: string\|null, downloadBytes: number, missingBytes: number, memoryBytes: number, width: number, height: number, frames: number, seconds: number, tokens: number }>`.

### `probeGpuMemory(adapter, bytes)`

True when the adapter's device gives `bytes` of buffers (in pieces no larger
than its limit), checked with an error scope and released at once.

## `sdk/video-gen/impl.js`

The text-to-video task where the model runs (a Worker). Wan 2.1 T2V 1.3B, a few-step distilled student, with ONNX Runtime Web on WebGPU: Nothing of the encoder stays loaded once the transformer loads; dispose() releases every session. Progress: ctx.report('running', { stage, index, count }).

### `FILES`

The files of the model, by role (references of registry/tasks.json).

## `sdk/video-gen/index.js`

Video from text in the browser, with Wan 2.1 T2V 1.3B (Wan-AI, Apache-2.0) distilled to a few steps, on WebGPU. Heavy: it downloads gigabytes once and needs a capable GPU, so ask `estimate()` first; it never pretends to run where it cannot. The model comes through the Elffuss model store, at pinned revisions; nothing of the prompt or the video leaves the browser.

### `supported()`

Whether this browser may run the task at all: WebGPU gives it an adapter. It
downloads nothing; `estimate()` says whether a given video fits this device.

Returns `Promise<boolean>`.

### `STAGES`

Stages a run reports, in order (`onProgress` events carry `stage`, `index`, `count`).

### `class TextToVideo`

Text to video. Runs in a Worker; the first `load()` or `run()` downloads the
model into the store (several gigabytes, once) and checks every file.

```js
import { TextToVideo, estimate } from '@elffuss/ai/video-gen';
const can = await estimate({ seconds: 2, size: '832x480' });   // { fits, reason, downloadBytes, missingBytes, … }
const t2v = new TextToVideo({ onProgress: p => console.log(p.stage, p.index, p.count) });
const { blob, mime, width, height, seconds, fps, seed } = await t2v.run(null, { prompt: 'a red fox in the snow', seconds: 2 });
await t2v.dispose();
```

`run(input, opts)`: `input` is ignored (pass null) or the prompt; `opts` is
`{ prompt, seconds, size, seed, steps, audio }`, every field JSON except
`audio` (`{ sampleRate, channels: Float32Array[] }`, fitted to the video).
Cancel with the `signal` of the constructor or of `run()`: the Worker is
stopped and every GPU buffer goes with it.

- `.constructor(options = {})`

### `generate(options = {})`

One video, then everything released: `await generate({ prompt, seconds, size, seed, steps })`.
The task's options (`onProgress`, `signal`, `store`, …) go in the same object.
This is the chat tool `video.generate`: its `args` are this object, unchanged.

Returns `Promise<{ blob: Blob, mime: string, width: number, height: number, seconds: number, fps: number, frames: number, seed: number, steps: number, model: string, device: string }>`.

## `sdk/video-gen/latent.js`

The latent video of Wan 2.1 and what the transformer reads from it. The VAE turns 1 + 4k frames of W × H pixels into 1 + k latent frames of 16 channels at W/8 × H/8; the transformer cuts each latent frame into 2 × 2 patches (one token each, 64 values). Patchify and unpatchify are plain reorderings, done here and not in the graphs, so the sampler works on a flat array in the latent's own order [16, F, H, W]. The rotary position tables and the timestep's sinusoid are computed here too, in double precision.

### `FPS`

Frames per second of Wan 2.1 videos.

### `LATENT_CHANNELS`

Channels of the latent.

### `TOKEN_VALUES`

Values per token (16 channels × 2 × 2 pixels of the latent).

### `DIM`

Hidden size and heads of the 1.3B transformer.

### `grid({ width, height, frames })`

Sizes of a generation: pixels, frames, latent and tokens.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `o` | `{ width: number, height: number, frames: number }` | width and height multiples of 16, frames 1 + 4k |

### `framesFor(seconds)`

Frames of a video of about `seconds` at 16 fps: 1 + 4k, at least 5.

### `patchify(z, g, f0 = 0, nf = g.f - f0)`

Tokens of latent frames [f0, f0 + nf) in the patch embedding's order: per token
(frame, row, column), its 64 values as (channel, dy, dx).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `z` | `Float32Array` | latent [16, F, H, W] |
| `g` | `{ f: number, h: number, w: number }` |  |
| `[f0]` | `number` | first frame |
| `[nf]` | `number` | frames |

### `unpatchify(tokens, g, f0 = 0, nf = g.f - f0, into = new Float32Array(16 * g.f * g.h * g.w))`

The transformer's output tokens (64 values as (dy, dx, channel)) written back
into latent frames [f0, f0 + nf) of `into` [16, F, H, W].

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | `Float32Array` |  |
| `g` | `{ f: number, h: number, w: number }` |  |
| `[into]` | `Float32Array` |  |

### `ropeTables(g, f0 = 0, nf = g.f - f0)`

Rotary tables of Wan's 3D position embedding for `nf` latent frames from
frame `f0`: per token, 64 angles (22 for time, 21 for rows, 21 for columns).

Returns `{ cos: Float32Array, sin: Float32Array }`: each [tokens, 64]

### `timeFrequencies(t)`

The timestep's sinusoid, 256 values (cosines then sines), as Wan computes it in float64.

## `sdk/video-gen/noise.js`

The Gaussian noise of a generation, drawn the same way in any language: every value comes from (seed, stream, index) through a 32-bit integer hash and the Box-Muller transform, so the browser and a reference run elsewhere start from the very same latent. A stream is one use of noise: 0 the starting latent, 1, 2, … the noise added back between steps.

### `hash32(x)`

A 32-bit integer hash (an avalanche mix of shifts and odd multiplications).

### `gaussian(seed, stream, count, { offset = 0, out = new Float32Array(count) } = {})`

`count` standard normal values of one stream, from value `offset` on.
Values come in pairs, so a run that starts at an odd offset recomputes the
pair it starts in; any slice equals the same slice of the whole stream.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `seed` | `number` | 32-bit seed |
| `stream` | `number` | which use of noise (0 the start, 1… the steps) |
| `count` | `number` | how many values |
| `[opts]` | `{ offset?: number, out?: Float32Array }` |  |

Returns `Float32Array`.

### `randomSeed()`

A seed for a generation when the caller gives none: 31 random bits.

## `sdk/video-gen/schedule.js`

Few-step sampling of distilled Wan students. Every student here predicts the rectified-flow velocity v at time t (x_t = (1 - t)·x0 + t·noise), and they are sampled the same way: estimate the clean latent x0 = x_t - t·v, then put fresh noise back at the next, smaller time. Only the list of times changes: The model receives t × 1000.

### Type `SamplerSpec`

```ts
{ kind: 'trigflow', sigmaMax: number, mid: number[] } | { kind: 'shifted', shift: number, list: number[] }
```

### `flowTimes(spec, steps)`

Flow times of a sampler for `steps` steps, from the first (near 1) down to 0.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `spec` | `SamplerSpec` |  |
| `steps` | `number` | 1 to the most the sampler has |

Returns `number[]`: steps + 1 times

### `step(x, v, t, tNext, noise)`

One step, in place: x ← (1 - tNext)·(x - t·v) + tNext·noise. With tNext = 0 it
leaves the clean estimate.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `Float32Array` | the current latent (overwritten) |
| `v` | `ArrayLike<number>` | the predicted velocity |
| `t` | `number` | current flow time |
| `tNext` | `number` | next flow time |
| `noise` | `ArrayLike<number> \| null` | fresh noise, needed when tNext > 0 |

## `sdk/video-gen/t5.js`

What the UMT5 encoder graphs need from JavaScript: the token embeddings, gathered from the 4-bit table (blocks of 32 with a scale and a zero each), and the relative-position buckets of T5's attention bias (bidirectional, 32 buckets, distances up to 128), as Wan's T5RelativeEmbedding computes them.

### `T5_DIM`

Width of the encoder.

### `T5_VOCAB`

Rows of the embedding table (umt5-xxl's padded vocabulary).

### `TEXT_LEN`

Length the transformer reads: the encoder's output padded with zeros.

### `ROW_BYTES`

Bytes of one row of the embedding table: 4-bit values, then fp16 scales, then 4-bit zeros (blocks of 32).

### `gatherEmbeddings(table, ids, { dim = T5_DIM, vocab = T5_VOCAB } = {})`

Embeddings of `ids`, [ids.length × 4096] float32, from the 4-bit table. A
row holds 2048 bytes of values (low nibble first), 128 fp16 scales and 64
bytes of zero points (low nibble first): value = (q - zero) × scale.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `table` | `ArrayBuffer\|Uint8Array` | `T5_VOCAB` rows of `ROW_BYTES` |
| `ids` | `number[]` |  |

### `relativeBuckets(L, { buckets = 32, maxDistance = 128 } = {})`

Relative-position buckets [L × L] (BigInt64Array, row q, column k) of a
bidirectional T5 attention bias.

### `padContext(hidden, L, { len = TEXT_LEN, dim = T5_DIM } = {})`

The encoder's output [L × 4096] padded with zeros to 512 rows (what Wan feeds the transformer).

## `sdk/video-gen/tokenizer.js`

The UMT5 tokenizer Wan 2.1 uses (google/umt5-xxl, the tokenizer.json in the Wan-AI repository): the prompt is cleaned the way Wan cleans it (ftfy's fixes that matter for typed text, HTML entities undone twice, runs of white space made one space), split at spaces into words that start with "▁", each word cut into the vocabulary's pieces by the Unigram model's best path (Viterbi), and "</s>" appended. No dependencies; the vocabulary comes from tokenizer.json.

### `cleanPrompt(text)`

The prompt as Wan's tokenizer wrapper cleans it (`whitespace_clean(basic_clean(text))`):
the subset of ftfy.fix_text that typed prompts meet (quotes, ligatures, full-width
forms, control characters, line breaks, NFC), HTML entities undone twice, white
space collapsed and trimmed.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` |  |

### `createTokenizer(json)`

A tokenizer from the parsed tokenizer.json of umt5-xxl.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `json` | `{ model: { type: string, vocab: [string, number][], unk_id: number } }` |  |
